Piece.description: Everything in a scene is a piece. Pieces nest: a piece's children belong to it.

pausable.description: Stops while the game is paused (pauseGame()). Turn it off for pause menus: this piece and everything inside it keep running.

find.doc: A child by name, or a deeper piece by path ("UI/Score"); nil if there isn't one.

findDeep.doc: The first piece with this name anywhere inside this one.

findChildOfType.doc: The first child of a type ("Sprite"), or nil.

isA.doc: True if the piece is of a type, or a type made from it.

add.doc: Adds a piece as the last child; returns it.

remove.doc: Takes the piece out of its parent now, without destroying it, so it can be added somewhere else.

spawn.doc: Makes a piece from a scene file or a piece type and adds it as a child: self:spawn("scenes/bullet.scene", { x = 10 }).

destroy.doc: Removes the piece and everything inside it at the end of the frame.

tag.doc: Gives the piece a tag, so smitten.scene.tagged(name) finds it and collisions can filter by it.

hasTag.doc: True if the piece has the tag.

hasAnyTag.doc: True if the piece has any of the tags in a comma-separated list: hasAnyTag("enemy, spikes").

is.doc: True if the piece has the tag or is of the type: other:is("enemy"), other:is("Body").

on.doc: Calls fn(...) whenever the piece's event happens ("pressed", "entered", ...). Returns a handle with :off().

emit.doc: Fires an event: calls the script's function of that name and every listener.

getPath.doc: The piece's path from the scene's root, like "Level/Player".

isAlive.doc: True while the piece is in the running scene and not destroyed.

ready.doc: The piece and everything inside it have joined the scene. The scene's root gets go()'s extra values.

update.doc: Every frame. dt is the time since the last frame, in seconds.

physicsUpdate.doc: 60 times a second, before bodies move. Use it for movement.

draw.doc: Draw extra things on top of the piece, in its own coordinates.

removed.doc: The piece is leaving the scene.

Group.description: A piece with a position. Use it to hold other pieces (they move with it) or to run a script.

y.description: Position, measured from the parent. y grows downwards.

rotation.description: Turn, clockwise: radians in code, degrees in the inspector.

visible.description: Show this piece and everything inside it.

tint.description: Multiplies the colors of this piece and everything inside it.

layer.description: Higher layers are drawn on top. Pieces on the same layer draw in scene order.

worldPosition.doc: Where the piece is in the scene (not measured from its parent): x, y.

setWorldPosition.doc: Moves the piece to a place in the scene.

toWorld.doc: A point measured from this piece, as a point in the scene.

fromWorld.doc: A point in the scene, measured from this piece.

lookAt.doc: Turns the piece to face a point in the scene.

distanceTo.doc: Distance in pixels to another piece or a point.

angleTo.doc: Angle in radians towards another piece or a point.

moveToward.doc: Moves at most distance pixels towards a point; true once it's there.

translate.doc: Moves the piece by an offset.

Timer.description: Counts down and calls tick() on its script and listeners. For spawn waves, cooldowns and delays.

running.description: Counting. On in the scene file means it starts with the scene.

loop.description: Keep ticking; off ticks once and stops.

Sprite.description: Draws a picture, or an animation from a .sprite file or a sprite sheet.

image.description: A picture (.png, .jpg) or a .sprite file with frames and animations.

animation.description: The animation to play, from the .sprite file.

speed.description: Animation speed: 2 is twice as fast.

columns.description: For a sprite sheet without a .sprite file: frames across.

rows.description: For a sprite sheet without a .sprite file: frames down.

centered.description: Center the picture on the piece's position (a .sprite file's origin wins).

play.doc: Plays an animation (or resumes the current one). restart starts it again from its first frame even if it's playing.

pause.doc: Stops the animation where it is; play() continues it.

stop.doc: Stops the animation and goes back to its first frame.

hasAnimation.doc: True if the .sprite file has an animation with this name.

animations.doc: The names of the .sprite file's animations, sorted.

getSize.doc: Width and height of one frame, in pixels.

getRect.doc: The rectangle the picture covers, in the piece's own coordinates: x, y, width, height.

finished.doc: A non-looping animation reached its last frame.

Shape.description: Draws a rectangle, circle, polygon or line. Good for prototypes, effects and games without art.

points.description: Corner points x1, y1, x2, y2, ...

filled.description: Fill the shape; off draws only its outline.

centered.description: Center the rectangle on the piece's position.

getRect.doc: The rectangle the shape covers, in the piece's own coordinates: x, y, width, height.

Text.description: Words in the game world, like a sign or a damage number. For scores and menus, use Label.

font.description: A .ttf/.otf font file, "pixel" for the built-in pixel font, or empty for the default font.

align.description: Lines up the text around the piece's position.

wrap.description: Wrap lines longer than this; 0 never wraps.

Tiles.description: A grid of tiles from a tileset, painted in the scene view. Tiles marked solid are walls and floors that bodies can't pass.

tileset.description: The .tileset file: a picture cut into tiles, with settings such as solid.

solid.description: Tiles marked solid block bodies. Off makes every tile just decoration.

getTile.doc: The tile number in a cell, or -1 if it's empty.

tileInfo.doc: The settings of a tile in the tileset (solid, name, ...).

cellAt.doc: The cell under a point in the scene: column, row.

cellPosition.doc: The scene position of a cell's top-left corner.

cellsWith.doc: A list of {column, row, tile} for every painted cell (or every cell with that tile).

fill.doc: Sets a rectangle of cells to one tile (-1 empties them).

tileAt.doc: The tile number under a point in the scene, or -1.

isSolid.doc: True if the cell's tile is marked solid (and solid is on).

neighbors.doc: The cells around one, as {column, row, tile} (tile -1 when empty): up, right, down, left, or all eight with diagonal.

cellCenter.doc: The scene position of a cell's center.

getTileSize.doc: The size of one cell in the scene: width, height.

getBounds.doc: The painted area in the scene: x, y, width, height (all 0 when empty).

Camera.description: Decides which part of the scene is on screen. Put it inside the player to follow them.

active.description: Use this camera. When several are active, the first in the scene wins.

smoothing.description: How gently it catches up: 0 sticks exactly, 5 glides.

target.description: A piece to follow, wherever the camera is in the scene (empty: the camera's own position).

offsetX.description: Looks this far right of what it follows.

offsetY.description: Looks this far below what it follows.

left.description: Don't show anything left of this (empty for no edge).

right.description: Don't show anything right of this.

follow.doc: Follows a piece (nil: back to target, or the camera's own position).

snap.doc: Jumps straight to what it follows, without smoothing (after a teleport).

setLimits.doc: Sets the edges it doesn't show past (nil for no edge).

limitTo.doc: Keeps the view inside the painted part of a Tiles piece.

makeCurrent.doc: Makes this the camera in use, turning the others off.

getView.doc: The part of the scene on screen: x, y, width, height.

screenToWorld.doc: A point on the screen, as a point in the scene.

worldToScreen.doc: A point in the scene, as a point on the screen.

Particles.description: Sprays particles: smoke, sparks, dust, rain, explosions.

burst.description: Make one burst of rate particles, then stop.

image.description: The particle picture; empty draws soft dots.

speedRandom.description: How much the speed varies (0 to 1).

spread.description: How far directions vary either side.

followPiece.description: Particles move with the piece instead of staying where they were born.

emit.doc: Makes count particles right now. emit("event", ...) still fires an event.

start.doc: Starts making particles (a burst makes its particles again).

stop.doc: Stops making particles; the ones already out live on.

restart.doc: Clears every particle and starts again.

getCount.doc: How many particles are out now.

finished.doc: The last particle is gone and no more are coming (after a burst or stop()). Good for destroy().

Body.description: Something solid: it bumps into other bodies and solid tiles. Pick how it moves: still (walls and floors), scripted (players and enemies you move in code with move()) or physics (crates and balls that fall, roll, get pushed and thrown). Put a Sprite or Shape inside it and its shape fits itself; it turns with the Body.

motion.description: Still never moves on its own (a script can still move it, and it carries what stands on it); scripted moves when its script calls move(), sliding along walls and up slopes; physics falls, bounces, tumbles and gets pushed.

shape.description: Auto fits the Sprites and Shapes inside it (a lone circle or polygon Shape exactly). Capsule is a rectangle with round ends, good for characters. None uses only its Hitboxes. Shapes turn and scale with the Body.

points.description: Corner points x1, y1, x2, y2, ... (up to 8 corners; a dent is filled in).

vx.description: Speed sideways. Scripted: what move() goes by. Physics: its speed now (set it to throw it).

vy.description: Speed down (negative is up). Scripted: what move() goes by. Physics: its speed now.

spin.description: How fast it turns (clockwise is positive). Scripted: move() turns it this fast.

slope.description: The steepest surface that still counts as ground: move() walks up it without sliding back.

mass.description: How heavy it is. A scripted body pushes physics bodies as hard as its mass against theirs allows.

friction.description: How much it grips what it touches: 0 is ice.

bounce.description: How much it bounces: 0 none, 1 forever.

gravity.description: How strongly gravity pulls it; 0 floats, -1 falls up.

drag.description: Air resistance: slows its movement down.

bullet.description: Checked continuously against other physics bodies too, so it can't pass through them however fast it goes. For small fast things.

asleep.description: Resting: it doesn't move until something touches or pushes it. Physics bodies fall asleep by themselves when they stop.

passThrough.description: Tags of things it doesn't bump into, like "ghost, pickup" ("tiles" for solid tiles).

move.doc: Moves by vx, vy for this step, sliding along walls, walking up slopes, standing on moving platforms and pushing physics bodies (scripted bodies). Speed into what it touches is taken off vx, vy.

moveBy.doc: Moves by an offset and stops at the first thing in the way; returns what it hit, or nil.

onGround.doc: True if the last move ended standing on something.

onWall.doc: True if the last move ran into a wall.

onCeiling.doc: True if the last move ran into a ceiling.

applyImpulse.doc: A sudden push (mass times change of speed), like a jump, a kick or a hit; at a point in the scene it also spins it. applyImpulse(0, -400) on a 1 kg body sends it up at 400 px/s.

applyForce.doc: Pushes steadily for this step (call it every physicsUpdate for wind or thrusters), at its center or at a point.

applyTorque.doc: Turns it steadily for this step (physics bodies).

grab.doc: Takes hold of it at a point in the scene, for dragTo(): a physics body is pulled there by a spring, so it swings and can be thrown.

dragTo.doc: Moves the grabbed point towards x, y.

drop.doc: Lets go after grab(); a physics body keeps its speed.

touching.doc: The first body or zone with a tag (or that piece) touching this one, or nil.

isTouching.doc: True if it touches a piece (a body, zone or Tiles) or anything with a tag.

contacts.doc: What it touches now: a list of {piece, x, y, nx, ny, impulse}, the normal pointing towards this body.

touchingTile.doc: The settings of a touching tile that has this setting (like "damage"), or nil.

getSize.doc: The size of the box around its shapes: width, height.

hit.doc: It started touching another body or solid tiles. contact has x, y (where), nx, ny (the direction from other to this body) and impulse (how hard).

Zone.description: An area that notices bodies and zones going in and out: pickups, checkpoints, danger. Nothing bumps into it. Still bodies aren't noticed.

shape.description: Auto fits the Sprites and Shapes inside it. Shapes turn and scale with the Zone.

points.description: Corner points x1, y1, x2, y2, ... (up to 8 corners).

detects.description: Only notices things with one of these tags (empty: everything).

active.description: Notice things going in and out.

inside.doc: A list of the bodies and zones inside it now.

touching.doc: The first body or zone with a tag (or that piece) inside it, or nil.

isTouching.doc: True if a piece (or anything with a tag) is inside it.

entered.doc: A body or zone came in.

Hitbox.description: An extra collision shape for the Body or Zone it's inside, for shapes auto can't make: an L shape, a sword's reach. It moves, turns and scales with its piece.

shape.description: The shape, placed and turned by the Hitbox's position and rotation.

points.description: Corner points x1, y1, x2, y2, ... (up to 8 corners).

Joint.description: Connects two bodies, or a body and the place where the Joint is: a pin, a weld, a rope, a spring, a rod, a slider, a wheel, or a mouse grip that pulls a body to wherever the Joint goes.

kind.description: Pin turns around the Joint; weld holds tight; rope keeps them at most length apart; spring pulls them towards length apart; distance keeps them exactly length apart; slider slides along the Joint's x direction; wheel turns and springs along the Joint's y direction; mouse pulls a towards the Joint.

b.description: The body it connects a to (empty: the place where the Joint is).

length.description: How far apart; 0 uses the distance when the joint is made.

spring.description: Springy: a pin or slider pulls back to where it started, a weld wobbles.

stiffness.description: How stiff the spring is: wobbles per second.

damping.description: How quickly the spring stops wobbling: 1 doesn't overshoot.

motor.description: Drive it: turn a pin or wheel, or move a slider, at motorSpeed.

motorSpeed.description: Radians per second (pin, wheel) or pixels per second (slider, distance).

motorStrength.description: The most torque (pin, wheel) or force (slider, distance) the motor uses.

limit.description: Keep a pin between minAngle and maxAngle, or a slider or wheel between lower and upper.

minAngle.description: The furthest a pin turns anticlockwise.

maxAngle.description: The furthest a pin turns clockwise.

lower.description: The furthest a slider or wheel goes back.

upper.description: The furthest a slider or wheel goes forward.

strength.description: The most force a mouse joint pulls with; 0 is plenty for the body's mass.

collide.description: The two bodies still bump into each other.

breakForce.description: Breaks (and sends broke) when pulled harder than this; 0 never breaks.

getAngle.doc: How far a pin has turned (radians).

getTranslation.doc: How far a slider has slid (pixels).

getLength.doc: How far apart a rope, spring or distance joint's ends are.

getSpeed.doc: How fast a pin turns or a slider slides.

getForce.doc: How hard the joint pulls now.

getTorque.doc: How hard the joint twists now.

broke.doc: It was pulled harder than breakForce and let go.

UI.description: The base of UI pieces: a rectangle on the screen, placed from a corner, an edge or the center.

anchor.description: What its position is measured from. Fill stretches over the whole screen (or the UI piece it's inside).

visible.description: Show this piece and everything inside it.

getRect.doc: Where it is on the screen now: x, y, width, height.

isHovered.doc: True while the mouse is over it.

hovered.doc: The pointer came over it (not Labels).

Label.description: Words on the screen: scores, timers, titles, dialog.

text.description: What it says. Change it from a script: text = `Score: {score}`.

font.description: A .ttf/.otf font, "pixel", or empty for the default font.

align.description: Lines up the text inside its rectangle.

valign.description: Lines up the text top to bottom.

outline.description: A dark outline, so it reads on any background.

Button.description: A button to click or tap. Its script gets pressed().

font.description: A font, or empty for the default.

autofocus.description: Has the keyboard focus when the scene starts: arrow keys and the d-pad move between buttons, accept presses. For menus.

focus.doc: Gives it the keyboard focus (arrow keys and the d-pad then move it between buttons; accept presses).

isFocused.doc: True while it has the keyboard focus.

pressed.doc: The button was clicked, tapped, or pressed with accept while focused.

Panel.description: A colored box behind other UI: a dialog, a HUD background.

pressed.doc: The panel was clicked or tapped (not on a button inside it).

Picture.description: A picture on the screen: an icon, a portrait, a logo.

fit.description: How the picture fills the rectangle.

pressed.doc: The picture was clicked or tapped.

Bar.description: A bar that fills up: health, loading, a countdown.

value.description: How full it is, between min and max.

Sound.description: Plays a sound or music: a .wav, .ogg or .mp3 file, or a .sfx or .song made in Smitten.

pitch.description: 1 is normal; 2 is an octave up.

play.doc: Plays the sound and returns the LÖVE Source playing it. Calling it again while it plays starts another copy (good for effects); a .song has one.

fadeIn.doc: Plays from silence up to its volume (or volume) over some seconds.

fadeOut.doc: Fades to silence, then stops; volume goes back to what it was.

seek.doc: Jumps to a time in the sound.

getDuration.doc: How long the sound is, in seconds.

finished.doc: The sound reached its end (not when looping).
